```{r}
#| label: native-defaults-setup
#| include: false
# medfit 0.14.0 warns once per session that fit_sem()'s fixed_x and meanstructure defaults change in 0.15.0.
# This hidden fit consumes that warning so the results below print on the 0.14 defaults without it.
invisible(withCallingHandlers(
  medfit::fit_sem("mediator1 ~ treatment\noutcome ~ mediator1 + treatment", data = medfit::mediation_demo),
  medfit_warning_default_change = function(w) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
))
```

Every model medfit can run, in one place. Find yours in the first table, then
open its page. For a one-page lookup of every function see the
[Reference Card](refcard.html); for short task recipes see the
[Cookbook](cookbook.html).

## Capabilities at a glance

| Model | Class | Engines and routes | Standard errors | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Simple | `MediationData` | `glm`, `regmedint`, `extract_mediation()` (`lm`/`glm`, lavaan), native | model, sandwich | [simple](model-simple.html) |
| Binary or count variables | `MediationData` | `glm` families | model, sandwich | [glm families](model-glm-families.html) |
| Treatment-by-mediator | `InteractionMediationData` | `glm`, `regmedint`, lavaan, native (`fit_sem()` with `x:m`) | model; closed form (`regmedint`) | [interaction](model-interaction.html) |
| Weighted | `MediationData` | `glm`; native `weights` | sandwich (HC3; native HC0-type) | [weights](model-weights.html) |
| Serial | `SerialMediationData` | `lm`/`glm` with `mediator_models`, lavaan, native via `fit_sem()` | model | [serial](model-serial.html) |
| Parallel | `ParallelMediationData` | `lm`/`glm`, lavaan, native via `fit_sem()` | model | [parallel](model-parallel.html) |
| Joint, with products | `JointMediationData` | `lm` fits | delta method, bootstrap | [joint](model-joint.html) |
| Cluster-level treatment (2-1-1) | `ClusterMediationData` | `lmer` fits or `engine = "lmer"` | model, Kenward-Roger (`"kr"`) | [cluster](model-cluster.html) |
| Latent mediator, constraints | `SEMFit`, then extracted | `fit_sem()`, `engine = "native"` | model, sandwich | [native](model-native.html), [latent](model-native-latent.html) |
| Categorical covariates (0.11.0) | `SEMFit`, then extracted | `fit_sem()` with a factor, character or logical column | model, sandwich | [categorical covariates](model-native-factors.html) |

Inference works on every row: delta-method intervals from `tidy()` and
`confint()`, and the parametric, nonparametric and plugin bootstrap (see
[Bootstrap Inference](bootstrap.html)).

::: {.callout-note}
## The native engine takes one mediator in `fit_mediation()`
`fit_mediation(engine = "native", model = )` accepts a single mediator. For
several mediators, fit the syntax with `fit_sem()` (see
[Native: several mediators and weights](model-native-multi.html)) and then call
`extract_mediation(fit, mediator = c(...), outcome = )`, with
`structure = "parallel"` for side-by-side mediators.
:::

## The `fit_mediation()` engines compared

The four engines answer different questions and do not return interchangeable numbers. Read the row for your engine
before you swap one for another.

| | `glm` (default) | `regmedint` | `lmer` | `native` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Estimation | `stats::glm()` for the mediator and outcome models | closed-form natural effects from the regmedint package | REML mixed models, a random cluster intercept in both | maximum-likelihood SEM from syntax (`model =`) |
| Outcome and mediator families | any `glm` family | a linear mediator model; the outcome may be logistic | Gaussian only | Gaussian only |
| Indirect effect | product of path coefficients, on the link scale when the link is not the identity | regmedint's natural indirect effect; equals the path product only for a linear mediator model and a unit treatment contrast (the adapter errors otherwise) | `a * b_between` (own and spillover parts in `decompose()`) | the path product from the fitted syntax |
| Case `weights` | yes | no | no | yes (weighted maximum likelihood) |
| `se_type = "sandwich"` | yes, HC3 | no (`"model"` only) | no (`"model"` or `"kr"`) | yes, HC0-type, a little smaller than HC3 in finite samples |
| Rows with missing values | dropped once, both models share the sample | dropped by the engine | dropped once | listwise, counted in `n_dropped` |
| Returns | `MediationData` or `InteractionMediationData` | the same two classes | `ClusterMediationData` | `SEMFit`, then `extract_mediation()` |

A weight or an SE type that an engine does not take is an error, not an ignored argument, so a silent change of
estimand is not possible through `fit_mediation()`. The estimand still differs where the table says so: a logistic
outcome through `glm` gives a path product on the log-odds scale, while `regmedint` gives a natural effect.

## What medfit does not run

- Treatment varying within clusters (1-1-1), and non-Gaussian outcomes or
  mediators in the cluster design.
- Four-way or joint decompositions with non-Gaussian models.
- Latent means (a free latent mean or intercept) on the native engine, and products with a latent variable.
  Observed intercepts and means (`y ~ 1`, `meanstructure =`) and the observed product `x:m` with its four-way
  decomposition are supported.
- Bayesian fits through `brms` (planned).

See [Methods and Formulas](methods.html) for the assumptions behind each model.
